terra.problem: The text does not identify the people as parents, say they carried the children, or say they came hoping for a blessing. It says they brought the children for Jesus to place His hands on them.
The text does not say that nobody got organized.
The text does not say whether the disciples carried anyone or what they wanted.
The text does not say Jesus pointed at the children or that the disciples shooed the children off. The disciples rebuked those who brought them.
The text does not say Jesus pointed at the children or describe anyone handing them a rulebook.
The text does not say Jesus was looking at the children when He said this.
The claim that a little child just receives with open hands adds an explanation that Jesus does not give here.
The text does not identify the people who brought the children as their parents or say how the children went home.
The explanation states that the man was serious without marking that as a guess. It also turns his running into sprinting.
The text does not say that asking the question was the whole reason the man came running.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer and promise, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation is a generic restatement and closely follows the same shape as the temple explanation.
The text says the man went away, but does not say he walked off in the other direction.
Saying the disciples had not seen it coming states an unreported thought as fact.
Jesus says many, but the explanation adds that this means not all.
The final sentence leaves out Jesus' qualifier that many who are first will be last.
